 Versus The State of Jharkhand ..... .... Respondent  --------
CORAM :
MR. JUSTICE RONGON MUKHOPADHYAY HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AMBUJ NATH

For the Appellant(s) : Mr. Indrajit Sinha, Advocate  : Mr. Akhouri Awinash Kumar, Advocate For the State : Mr. Manoj Kr. Mishra, A.P.P For the Informant : Mr. Chandrajit Mukherjee, Advocate  --------
07/ Dated 09.07.2025 I.A. No. 5912 of 2025 Heard Mr. Indrajit Sinha, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Manoj Kr. Mishra, learned A.P.P on behalf of the State, assisted by Mr. Chandrajit Mukherjee, learned counsel appearing for the informant.
This interlocutory application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 04 of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years along with a fine of Rs. 20,000/- for the offence under Section 4 of the POCSO Act.
It has been alleged that the appellant had abducted the victim on 07.02.2020 and had taken her on a motorcycle to a lonely place at village Nawadih, where she was subjected to rape.
Subsequently, on the assurance of marriage, the appellant had continued to sexually abuse the victim and had also taken some nude photographs of the victim.

sentences.text: Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that initially, a complaint case was instituted which was sent to the police under Section 156 (3) Cr.

P.C. It has further been submitted that the age of the appellant at the time of the occurrence was 17 years and the appellant was also a minor at the time of incident and the evidence of the victim as well as the photographs which have been exhibited would clearly reveal a love affair between the appellant and the victim.

Learned counsel appearing for the informant has submitted that as per the evidence of P.W.5 who is the father of the victim, nude photographs were sent on his mobile, to which, Mr. Indrajit Sinha,
learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was not convicted under the Information Technology Act.

Learned counsel for the appellant has also submitted that though in the Fardbeyan of the victim, she had mentioned about being abducted on a motorcycle by the appellant, but the same does not find place in her 164 Cr.P.C. statement as well as in her evidence before the Court.
On consideration of the fact that there appears to be love affair between the appellant and the victim and the contradictions which has appeared in the fardbeyan of the victim as well as in her 164 Cr.P.C. statement as also in her evidence as P.W.1., we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during the pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Spl. Judge, POCSO Act, Jamtara in connection with POCSO Case No.
27/2022, arising out of Narayanpur P.S. Case No. 96/2022.
The aforesaid I.A. stands allowed and disposed of.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Ambuj Nath, J.) BS-Saurav/-
